Hence, a developmental disorder was suspected as the cause of the rootless teeth. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of DD was made. findings.label: Abnormal root morphology with malformed roots

panels.rationale: This is a panoramic radiograph of a patient diagnosed with Dentinal Dysplasia Type I. The caption and text explicitly mention findings highly characteristic of the condition, including root development being incomplete, second molars being unerupted with no root formation, and other unerupted teeth having short, blunted, and malformed roots with obliterated pulp chambers. These findings directly correspond to the pathology of dentin dysplasia. [raw subtype: Dentinal dysplasia type I]
panels.attribution_text: Ozer et al. Dentinal dysplasia type I: a case report with a 6-year followup.. Case reports in dentistry 2013. doi:10.1155/2013/659084. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.

in_text_mentions: In the radiographic examination, there was a radiolucent cystic lesion at right maxilla, first permanent molars and incisors were erupted, and the root development was incomplete. The permanent second molars were unerupted and had no root formation, while the other unerupted permanent teeth had short, blunted, and malformed roots with obliterated pulp chambers, and bone below the teeth showed well-defined margins (Figure 1).

There was second grade mobility in 64, 26 and 36 without the history of trauma and infection.
